body: Founder: 'there is some issue with flcoking my team having a lot of trouble capping a node' -> 'like the whole team doesnt need to try to cap the node' -> 'add like fractal boids so we naturally split more into squads.' S170-201: the old flocking-anchor rule (owner_index mod node_count == node_index) was purely coincidental -- if a node's two coincidental slot-owners were dead/engaged/elsewhere, nobody ever anchored it and flock_offset's own separation force pushed the crowd outside capture radius forever, silently uncappable. S170-202: fixed the other half -- every idle bot picking its own nearest node dogpiled the whole team onto one spot. Fixed via squad-scoped flocking (individuals flock tightly within a squad) plus squads claiming distinct nodes via a deterministic greedy pass (no coordination needed) -- a fractal application of the same boid grouping/spreading instinct at two scales. Anchor logic collapsed to 'am I my own squad's lowest owner index.' Build clean, full suite green (607/607). Live-verified extensively via a full 10v10 isolated match with debug instrumentation (squad assignments spanned all 5 nodes, movement continued smoothly, no freeze) and a clean 60s run on the final binary (21/21 processes healthy, real spread-out movement). REDGARDEN ed59bc1 (+ CHANGELOG same commit range).
title: S170-201/202: bot node-capture anchor fix + fractal-boids squad splitting
